# MASTER PROMPT - UC1 Architecture and Design Stage (conversation 3 of 3)

(Paste this prompt first, then paste the full contents of UC1_Stage3_Handoff.json in the same message or immediately after. No other attachment is needed.)

## 1. Your role
Act as SAP Commerce solution architect, Spartacus/Angular architect, AI orchestration architect, security/privacy reviewer and technical writer. Stages 1 (product discovery) and 2 (technical research) are complete and captured in the JSON. You produce the detailed architecture, technical design and the Claude Code implementation prompt. You do not write production code.

## 2. Inputs and rules
- The JSON is authoritative. product_definition carries the approved scope, 43-capability catalogue, scenarios, principles, decisions D01-D37 and open questions. coding_convention_reference, protected_decisions, research findings, feasibility, answers, spikes, risks and decisions_needing_owner_approval are included.
- Protected decisions must not change without product-owner approval. Where your design needs to touch one, list it under owner approvals with evidence and options; never change it silently.
- The Coding Convention Reference is mandatory. Preserve it and carry it, complete, into your output. The implementation prompt must instruct Claude Code to inspect the owner's supplied examples and follow them. Request clearer examples for anything marked unknown (examples_needed_from_owner).
- Keep verified facts, assumptions and recommendations visibly separate. Re-verify any evidence marked 'Secondary source only' or 'Not verified' before depending on it. Provider terms and platform versions may have changed since 2026-11-13.
- Research recommendations are proposals until the owner confirms them. Start with decisions_needing_owner_approval (A1-A14): confirm defaults in one brief round, then proceed.

## 3. Mission and required outputs
1. Architecture overview (extensions, layers, SPIs/gateways, runtime flow for streaming, orchestration, sanitisation, audit, configuration, pack switching) with diagrams.
2. Technical design: item types and Backoffice configuration, DTO beans, conceptual-to-concrete OCC contracts (including streaming events and non-streaming fallback), tool catalogue contracts, workflow templates per intent and scenario, DAO/FlexibleSearch design following the supplied conventions, provider adapter design, sanitisation design, prompt and schema design, response contract, frontend component and state design, theming, accessibility, ImpEx/pack generator design, test strategy, deployment and configuration.
3. Capability-to-design traceability for all 43 IDs and ten scenarios SC-01..SC-10.
4. Spike plan (S1-S8) with pass/fail criteria and the design branches each outcome triggers.
5. The Claude Code implementation prompt: staged build plan, repository layout, step-by-step prompts, acceptance checks, and the explicit instruction to inspect the supplied examples and follow the conventions.
6. Open items and owner approvals still outstanding.

## 4. Method
Work section by section; ask the product owner one focused question at a time only when a decision is genuinely theirs; otherwise recommend a default and continue. Search current documentation for any API, version or provider term you rely on and label it Verified, Assumption or Recommendation with source and date.

## 5. Final instruction
Be rigorous and honest, keep enterprise execution secure and controlled, and keep AI as interpreter and communicator with SAP Commerce Java as the executor of record.

items.decision: Delivery: public GitHub repo, drop-in module for client OCC/facade/core layers; no secrets/real data/client-specific models.
Demo runs on owner's local SAP Commerce with seeded dummy products, orders and carts.
Add to Cart targets a clearly labelled placeholder purchase list; real cart integration deferred; checkout in storefront; AI never places orders.
Baseline persona: dealer / B2B customer buyer only. Approvers, admins, sales reps are roadmap.
Search supports four request styles: by code, description/keywords, use case, constraints.
Search is deterministic and backend-controlled; AI extracts parameters and judges relevance; price/stock constraints evaluated in backend.
Conversation memory is session-only, tied to the browser tab; no persisted chat history.
Customer-linked interest events stored in a dedicated custom table; enabled by default with a visible notice; per-client toggle; default retention 90 days (configurable).
Experience is a full-page ChatGPT/Claude-style interface inside the storefront (not a pop-up), with a welcome panel of proactive suggestions.
Order tracking uses Commerce-held data only; carrier lookups deferred.
Replenishment is simple rule-based in baseline; enhancement later.
Purchase-pattern change detection is in the baseline; shown as labelled observations with numbers.
Every capability is individually enable/disable and configurable via Backoffice runtime configuration (config item types).
Cross-sell and bundles use deterministic logic; AI explains.
Knowledge/FAQ answers come only from admin-configured approved content.
Multilingual is toggleable: translate input to English, process, translate output back. Identifiers never translated.
Model provider and model are configurable per task across Gemini, Anthropic and OpenAI; providers can be switched on/off. Demo uses free Gemini plus OpenAI.
API keys live in secure properties (local.properties gitignored / environment / Cloud secret); project.properties holds safe defaults only; Backoffice holds references, toggles and routing.
Proactive welcome panel is in the baseline.
Attribute-based comparison and compatibility via a configurable attribute are in the baseline.
Reorder from a previous order is in the baseline.
Ten signature demonstration scenarios.
Business recommendation controls: toggles/weights per recommendation type plus an admin-set priority/margin attribute; margin never sent to LLM or customers.
Quantity recommendations (history-based) and basket optimisation are in the baseline.
Product cards: AI returns product IDs only; backend hydrates price/images; modern polished UI; customer-specific prices shown, never passed to the LLM.
Stock is hardcoded demo data (labelled) with a placeholder hook for live stock.
Off-topic questions are redirected; unsupported requests are declined transparently.
Live step indicators plus streamed, animated final answer.
Thumbs up/down feedback in baseline, stored as metadata only.
Baseline suggests contacting the account manager (configurable text) when unresolved; full human handoff workflow is roadmap.

Industry packs (tyres/auto parts, paints/coatings, cement/building materials, plywood/wood panels, electrical) with seed-data generators in the repo, live switching via configuration with data coexisting, theme and terminology changes.
Orders visible: logged-in user's own orders only; unit-level access is roadmap with 'future scope' code comments.
Replenishment uses the individual user's history only; unit-level is roadmap with 'future scope' comments.
Quick Order, budget planner, substitution, natural-language order search, 'Why this?' panel, editable purchase list are baseline; photo search and voice are roadmap.
Full-response target <=10 seconds with progress shown; per-customer usage caps in baseline (configurable).
Coding conventions come from owner-validated sample code (patterns binding; sample names are placeholders). Mark future-scope extension points with comments.

execution_and_orchestration_principles: AI is not the execution layer. AI interprets, reasons, orchestrates and communicates; backend Java executes and retrieves.

The LLM never generates SQL/FlexibleSearch for execution, never accesses the database, never executes arbitrary Java, never invents tools/APIs, never accesses another customer's data, never invents availability, price, order status or facts, never performs transactions without backend authorisation and customer approval.
Authorisation is always enforced by backend code using existing SAP Commerce authentication/authorisation. No separate authentication mechanism.
Agents propose the next step; backend validates it against a predefined tool catalogue and permitted workflow. Not every capability needs an AI agent; deterministic Java is preferred where suitable.
Product/order references flow as IDs: AI returns IDs only; backend hydrates data, prices and images and sends them to the front end. Prices and margin/priority data are never sent to the LLM.
Responses are grounded in retrieved data; unknown or unsupported requests are stated transparently.
Privacy-first: data minimisation, sanitisation (including for translation calls), reverse mapping only inside the trusted backend.
Every capability is individually toggleable and configurable (Backoffice runtime configuration).
Customer stays in control: Add to Cart goes to a clearly labelled placeholder list; checkout stays in the normal storefront; AI never places orders.
Historical facts are clearly distinguished from predictions/estimates.
Flow: message -> intent -> context -> action selection -> backend execution -> result analysis -> further tool/agent invocation -> consolidated response.

Support agent-to-agent, agent-to-tool, tool-to-agent hand-offs; sequential and parallel execution; context preservation; structured intermediate responses; conditional next steps; clarification; controlled retries/fallbacks; maximum execution limits.
ai_responsibilities: Understand requests, identify intent and context, extract keywords/parameters, interpret requirements, propose the next permitted tool/agent, analyse and summarise returned results, compare retrieved products, explain recommendations, consolidate results, generate responses, ask clarifying questions, translate when enabled.
backend_responsibilities: Define tools and contracts; validate AI parameters; decide whether actions are permitted; execute predefined Java/DAO/FlexibleSearch; apply business rules and calculations; enforce authentication, authorisation and customer isolation; validate transactional operations; sanitise before external model calls; validate AI responses; hydrate IDs into data/prices/images; maintain audit logs; evaluate price and stock constraints; store Backoffice configuration.
data_privacy_requirements: Send the LLM only what the current task needs (data minimisation).

Avoid exposing personal data, customer details, confidential commercial information, internal identifiers, supplier information, unnecessary order details, sensitive pricing and other customers' data.
Sanitisation layer: temporary references, masking, attribute removal, controlled backend mappings; restore references only inside the trusted backend. Random tokens do not guarantee anonymity.
Apply sanitisation to every external model call including translation.
Prices and margin/priority data never go to the LLM; sensitive calculations (budget eligibility, totals) happen in backend Java.
Validate AI output (product/order references and tool results) against trusted backend data before returning it.
Interest events: structured, backend-written, no raw chat text, notice shown, default 90-day retention.
Verify provider data-use terms (notably free-tier APIs) before recommending them for client data.
security_requirements: Controlled tool execution through a predefined catalogue only.
Customer data isolation; logged-in user's own data only in baseline.
Hallucination mitigation through grounding and ID validation.
Tool permission validation by backend on every proposed step.
Execution limits, retries and fallbacks; error handling; sensitive data redaction.
Secure configuration: keys in secure properties/env/Cloud secrets; never in source control.
audit_requirements: Log session/conversation reference, intent classification, confidence, agent hand-offs, tool selections and outcomes, errors and rejected operations, timestamps, model/provider info and token usage.
Do not log full prompts, personal information or confidential records indiscriminately.
Configurable retention and access policies; monitoring of failures and usage.

legend.feasible_with_change: Build with the stated change or owner approval
legend.not_recommended: None of the 43 capabilities is rejected outright; not-recommended elements are listed below

items.name: Full-page conversational experience
items.reason: Streaming/step events are not an OOTB OCC pattern. Use a custom OCC-extension endpoint returning SSE over POST (fetch-based Angular client, bearer token) plus a non-streaming fallback. CCv2 ingress/CDN buffering is unverified (spike S1). Mark the route client-side-rendered only.

items.name: Intent understanding and clarification
items.reason: One schema-constrained decision call (intent, confidence, parameters, proposed next step), validated by backend against catalogue and enabled capabilities. Can be merged with translate-in to save a call.

items.name: Rich response components
items.reason: IDs-only contract; backend hydrates and applies a provenance check (every ID must have appeared in this turn's tool results and pass permission checks). Components are presentational Angular.

items.name: Session-only conversation context
items.reason: Hold context in browser sessionStorage; backend stays stateless and re-validates and sanitises at egress on every call; clear on logout event. Client-supplied context is untrusted input.

items.name: Multilingual conversation
items.reason: Feasible, but serial detect+translate+classify+compose+translate-out threatens the 10s target. Merge detect/translate/classify into one call, keep static UI labels in Spartacus i18n, protect identifiers with placeholders. Free-tier Gemini only for synthetic demo data (E01); paid terms needed for client data and likely for EEA/UK/CH (E03). Optional compose-in-language variant would touch D17 (needs owner approval).

items.name: Off-topic redirect, honest limits, contact fallback
items.reason: Intent routing plus configurable fallback text; add deterministic guardrail list so over-refusal can be tuned.

items.name: Thumbs up/down feedback
items.reason: Separate Feedback item type, no free text, keyed by responseId and audit reference.

items.name: 'Why this?' transparency panel
items.reason: Trace must be a whitelisted DTO built from tool metadata (sources, windows, thresholds), never from ranking weights, margin, prompts or model text. Template-first explanations; LLM phrasing optional to save latency.

items.name: Natural-language product search
items.reason: Backend maps extracted keywords/filters onto a whitelist of configured attributes using parameterised FlexibleSearch (convention-compliant). Large catalogues need an optional Solr candidate provider behind the same SPI. Relevance judging sends product text only, never price or margin.

items.name: Guided discovery, categories and filters
items.reason: Category tree plus facet counts through the same candidate-provider SPI; facets per pack from pack attribute mapping.

items.name: Product Q&A from catalogue data
items.reason: getProductDetails returns an approved-field DTO; answer must cite fields; missing data is stated.

items.name: Attribute-based product comparison
items.reason: Deterministic comparison table from configured comparison attributes; AI text validated against table values.

items.name: Compatibility via configurable attribute
items.reason: Deterministic compatibility check on the configured attribute; unverifiable cases return 'cannot verify'.

items.name: Alternatives, similar products and substitution
items.reason: Deterministic similarity (same category + attribute proximity rules); stock via placeholder hook (D27).

items.name: Budget-based discovery
items.reason: Backend evaluates customer-specific price eligibility and returns approved IDs only. Cap candidate set before price lookups for performance. Budget stated by the dealer in chat is user input, not backend price data.

items.name: Product cards with Add to Cart (placeholder list)
items.reason: Spec says backend 'maintains' the placeholder list but D07 forbids server-side persistence. Keep the list in browser sessionStorage; backend validates, prices and checks it on each call. Clearly label as demo list.

items.name: Editable session purchase list
items.reason: Client-held list survives refresh in tab session; edits validated by backend before any AI use.

items.name: Quick Order from typed or pasted list
items.reason: Deterministic grammar/regex first pass; LLM only for residual messy lines; every line validated by backend (code, alias, normalised code, description search, clarification).

items.name: Budget purchase planner
items.reason: Java allocation (bounded knapsack in minor units / priority greedy) with totals computed in backend; exclusions explained.

items.name: Quantity recommendations
items.reason: Median/recent-mean quantity from the user's history; labelled as estimate.

items.name: Basket optimisation
items.reason: Deterministic checks over list, history and pending orders; each flag carries its data trace.

items.name: Reorder from a previous order
items.reason: Order lookup scoped to the logged-in customer through standard customer-account order retrieval; availability and substitution via PD-06.

items.name: Order retrieval, status and tracking (Commerce-held data)
items.reason: Customer-scoped lookups of order, consignment and delivery data held in Commerce. Customer is bound from the security context, never from AI output.

items.name: Natural-language order search
items.reason: Validated filter contract (date range, status, amount with currency) executed by parameterised queries following the supplied DAO convention.

items.name: Order summaries and order FAQs
items.reason: Summaries generated from backend DTO; FAQ from KN-01; numeric slots filled by backend.

items.name: Rule-based replenishment detection
items.reason: Per-user, per-product median inter-order gap and typical quantity with minimum-order threshold; due/overdue flags; configurable window.

items.name: Pending-order awareness
items.reason: Open-order statuses configurable; quantities netted from suggestions.

items.name: Proactive welcome panel
items.reason: Compute deterministically on page open; framing text template-first with optional cached LLM phrasing so welcome panel does not wait on a model.

items.name: Purchase-pattern change detection
items.reason: Trailing-mean vs recent-orders comparison with minimum sample and percentage threshold; observation text states numbers and no causes.

items.name: Suggested repeat-order list
items.reason: Assembles RI-01/RI-02 output into the client-held purchase list; customer approves each addition.

items.name: Cross-sell and complementary products
items.reason: Co-purchase counts (support/confidence) plus category rules, computed on demand with caching at demo scale; precompute job is an extension point for large order volumes.

items.name: Bundle suggestions
items.reason: Bundles derived from CI-01 patterns and rules; suppress when data is sparse.

items.name: Business recommendation controls
items.reason: Store priority/margin in a separate UC1 item type referencing the product (not an extra ProductModel attribute); ranker consumes it in Java after the LLM stage; trace builder whitelists fields so it can never leak.

items.name: Customer-linked interest events
items.reason: CI-04 says the AI classifies events. Recommend AI may only suggest an enumerated event type; backend decides and writes. 'Requested-but-not-found' must store a normalised category/attribute token, not free text. Enabled-by-default consent needs per-market legal review (D08 unchanged).

items.name: Approved FAQ and policy content
items.reason: Small approved corpus per pack: lexical retrieval, LLM selects entry IDs only, backend returns the approved text; no vector store in baseline.

items.name: Backoffice runtime configuration
items.reason: Feasible with custom Configuration items plus layered defaults. D13 says every capability is toggleable, but toggling PL-01, PL-03, PL-04 or PL-05 off conflicts with security requirements. Recommend fail-closed semantics (disabling sanitisation blocks external model calls). Needs owner approval because D13 is protected.

items.name: Per-task multi-provider model routing
items.reason: Own thin provider adapters over java.net.http.HttpClient + Jackson (matches supplied convention, avoids vendor SDK classpath conflicts); keys by alias from secure properties.

items.name: Sanitisation layer
items.reason: Guarantee holds for backend-supplied data; user-typed free text can only be masked best-effort. Reword acceptance criterion accordingly and warn users not to type personal data.

items.name: Tool catalogue and controlled orchestrator
items.reason: Own lightweight plan-validate-execute orchestrator with workflow templates per intent, bounded LLM branching, parallel independent tools and hard step/time limits.

items.name: Audit and observability
items.reason: Structured audit events through a dedicated logger (metadata only); optional DB-backed audit item as an extension point. Retention then follows the log platform.

items.name: Per-customer usage caps
items.reason: DB-backed counter per customer per period (multi-node safe), written in batches; graceful message at cap.

items.name: Industry packs
items.reason: Single base site and store; packs separated by root categories, pack config item and pack dealers. 'Live' switch = config change applied after short cache TTL plus page reload (SC-10 already says reload). Dealer identity per pack is an owner decision.

items.name: Extension points
items.reason: Spring-registered SPIs (Tool, Agent, Workflow, Rule, Gateway) discovered by bean type; core code unchanged when a client adds a tool.

not_recommended_elements: Using free-tier Gemini for any real client or dealer data
Letting the AI classify and write interest events directly (CI-04)
Streaming unvalidated model text to the user
Executing or constructing queries from model output (already excluded)
Storing margin/priority as a ProductModel or classification attribute

sap_commerce.extension_pattern: OCC extension from yocc template for endpoints; separate core/facades/backoffice/sampledata extensions; follow Controller -> Facade -> Service -> DAO with the supplied naming (interfaces + Default* implementations, *Data and *WsDTO beans in XML, @Resource injection).
sap_commerce.data_access: Parameterised FlexibleSearch constants per supplied DAO convention for orders, history and candidate search; PagedFlexibleSearchService for paged order search; customer always passed into DAO and filtered in the query. Optional Solr adapter for large catalogues behind a candidate-provider SPI.
sap_commerce.model_reuse: Product, Order/OrderEntry, Consignment, B2BCustomer, Category, classification features for industry attributes. Custom types only the six in answer 5.
sap_commerce.configuration: Layered: project.properties safe defaults -> local.properties/env/Cloud secrets -> Backoffice items (non-secret) -> service with short-TTL cache invalidated on save. Backoffice screens via *-backoffice-config.xml.
sap_commerce.packs_and_seed: Generators (script + manifest per pack) emit deterministic ImpEx; loaded by @SystemSetup hooks with per-pack options; order dates generated relative to load time so rhythms (e.g. 30-day) stay current.
alternatives_considered: Standalone web app (own security, high coupling)

frontend.route: Auth-guarded Angular route delivered as a lazy-loaded Spartacus feature library, CSR only; CMS-driven page variant optional later (SmartEdit).
frontend.streaming: Fetch-based POST stream reader with Spartacus token; step indicators and text in ARIA live regions; reduced-motion respected.
frontend.theming: Pack theme tokens (CSS custom properties) from config endpoint, scoped to the chat container.
frontend.components: Presentational components per block type; media via Spartacus media component; static labels via Spartacus i18n.
frontend.version_note: Verified: 2211.36-43 is Angular 19 / Node 22 (E10). Owner's actual version is unknown.
frontend.accessibility: Target WCAG 2.1 AA for the route; core storefront alone claims about 90% coverage (E20).

ai_orchestration.pattern: Hybrid: intent -> workflow template (deterministic pipelines for the ten scenarios) with bounded LLM-proposed branching among allowed tools; 'agents' are role-specific prompts (decision, relevance, composer, translator) run through one provider abstraction.
ai_orchestration.provider_abstraction: Own thin REST adapters; provider-neutral schema-constrained 'decision' and 'composition' calls instead of provider-specific tool loops (E08).
ai_orchestration.routing: Per-task config: small fast model for translate/classify, mid model for relevance and composition; fallback chain; timeouts and retries from config; token counters.
ai_orchestration.grounding: Evidence packs only; closed-world prompts; ID provenance check; numeric slots filled by backend; compare AI text with table values; unknown -> say so.
ai_orchestration.multilingual: Merged detect+translate+classify; identifier placeholders (codes, order numbers, brands); translate-out only for dynamic prose; static labels via i18n.

data_intelligence.search: Whitelisted attributes from pack mapping; classification-system features for industry attributes; FlexibleSearch default, Solr optional.
data_intelligence.recommendations: Co-occurrence (support/confidence), category rules, business ranker applied last.
data_intelligence.replenishment: Median inter-order gap per product (minimum orders), last/median quantity, due = last order + gap, overdue ratio; pending orders netted.
data_intelligence.pattern_change: Recent N orders vs trailing mean, percentage threshold, minimum sample; no causal claims.
data_intelligence.budget: Bounded knapsack in minor currency units; explain exclusions.
data_intelligence.quick_order: Grammar first, LLM for leftovers, backend validation ladder.
data_intelligence.faq: Lexical retrieval over approved entries; LLM returns entry IDs only.

security_governance.isolation: Bind customer from security context; ignore or reject userId mismatch; supplied sample allows ROLE_TRUSTED_CLIENT and ROLE_CUSTOMERMANAGERGROUP on /users/{userId}: confirm intended roles (owner).
security_governance.prompt_injection: Privilege separation: any model call that reads untrusted text (product text, FAQ, order notes, user text) has no tool authority and outputs only IDs/enums; delimit untrusted content; strip instruction-like patterns; validate outputs (OWASP LLM01/05/06).
security_governance.sanitisation: Field classification, masking, request-scoped token maps, re-check outbound payload against allow-list; free text best-effort.
security_governance.keys: Keys only in local.properties (gitignored), environment or Cloud secrets; Backoffice holds aliases; add secret scanning and push protection in the public repo.
security_governance.audit: Metadata-only structured events per PL-05, no prompts or personal data.
security_governance.limits: Step caps, time caps, per-customer caps, input length caps (OWASP LLM10).

operations.reliability: Timeouts, bounded retries for idempotent calls, circuit breaker, fallback model chain, partial-result responses with honest notice.
operations.testing: Unit tests for deterministic tools; recorded-fixture provider contract tests; golden-set intent and multilingual evals; injection corpus; isolation tests (SC-06); Angular unit and e2e; load test with fake provider. Owner has not supplied test examples.
operations.deployment: CCv2 extension packaging; separate storefront build with matching Node/Angular; gate release on spikes S1-S8.
operations.cost: Per-task routing, context trimming, caching of welcome panel and translations of static text, usage caps.

answers_to_specific_questions.question: Where should session context live?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: Browser sessionStorage (tab-scoped), sent as a bounded context envelope with each request; backend stays stateless. Sanitise at egress on every model call; token maps are request-scoped and discarded. Clear on Spartacus logout event.
alternatives: Server-side short-lived cache keyed by session (better token control and tamper resistance, but needs sticky or shared cache on multi-node CCv2 and risks contradicting 'no transcript stored server-side')
answers_to_specific_questions.label: Recommendation (assumption: sessionStorage semantics to be confirmed in spike S1)

answers_to_specific_questions.question: How to transport streaming and step progress through OCC and render in Spartacus?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: Custom OCC extension endpoint (POST, text/event-stream) built on Spring ResponseBodyEmitter/SseEmitter with heartbeat and explicit timeout. Events: step_started, step_completed, block, text_delta, done, error. Angular client uses fetch streaming with the Spartacus bearer token (EventSource cannot send Authorization). Validate-then-reveal: backend validates and hydrates composed output before streaming text, so users never see unvalidated claims. Non-streaming fallback: the sample-style POST /chat returning one WsDTO.
alternatives: NDJSON over POST (simpler parsing, same buffering risk)
Polling: POST creates a run, GET events (works through any proxy, higher latency)
answers_to_specific_questions.label: Recommendation; CCv2 behaviour is a GAP (E14), spike S1 mandatory
answers_to_specific_questions.touches_protected: D29 satisfied (live steps + animated streamed answer)

answers_to_specific_questions.question: How to model industry packs so data coexists and the experience switches live?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: One base site and base store; one product catalog (or catalogs on the same store) with a root category per pack; pack = Configuration/ConfigEntry item holding root categories, attribute mappings, terminology, sample prompts, theme tokens; per-pack demo dealers plus one all-packs demo dealer; every tool scopes by the active pack resolved in backend. Switch = change active pack config, cache TTL, reload.
alternatives: One base site per pack (hard isolation but five storefront contexts, no single live switch)
Separate catalogs per pack on one store (cleaner scoping, more ImpEx and sync work)
answers_to_specific_questions.label: Assumption (E19), spike S5
answers_to_specific_questions.touches_protected: D32 consistent; dealer identity needs owner input

answers_to_specific_questions.question: Current data-use/retention terms and compatibility with privacy-first positioning?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: Free-tier Gemini: content used to improve Google products and may be human-reviewed (E01) -> acceptable only for synthetic demo data, NOT for client guidance. Paid Gemini (billing-enabled project): not used for improvement (E02). OpenAI API: no training by default (secondary E06), abuse logs up to 30 days, ZDR by approval, set store=false (E05). Anthropic API: no training, deletion within 30 days with ZDR by arrangement; a 7-day claim conflicts (E07). Add a configuration guard: provider tier flag plus a 'synthetic data only' mode that refuses free-tier providers outside demo sites.
answers_to_specific_questions.label: Verified (see evidence ledger) + Recommendation
answers_to_specific_questions.touches_protected: D18 (demo uses free Gemini) stays valid for synthetic data; guard needs owner approval

answers_to_specific_questions.question: Which custom item types are minimally needed; can events and feedback share one?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: Minimum six: UC1Configuration, UC1ConfigEntry (typed by enum: toggle, threshold, prompt, terminology, provider route, pack, FAQ), UC1InterestEvent, UC1Feedback, UC1ProductBusinessAttribute, UC1UsageCounter. Audit via structured logs (optional item later). Events and feedback should NOT share a table: D08 requires a dedicated interest-event table and the two have different privacy lifecycles (customer-linked 90-day retention vs anonymous metadata). Share a Java base class and purge service instead. A shared type with discriminator is possible but needs owner approval.
alternatives: Dedicated UC1IndustryPack and UC1FaqEntry types (stronger typing, +2 types)
Single UC1Signal type with discriminator (fewer types; conflicts with D08 wording)
answers_to_specific_questions.label: Recommendation

answers_to_specific_questions.question: Where should the business priority/margin attribute live?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: Separate item type UC1ProductBusinessAttribute referencing the product (restricted Backoffice permission group). Avoid ProductModel extension (alters client's items.xml, breaks drop-in) and avoid classification features (exported to feeds/Solr, high leak risk). Ranking runs in Java after the LLM stage; trace and prompt builders use whitelisted DTOs that cannot carry the field.
alternatives: ProductModel attribute (simplest, couples to client type system)
answers_to_specific_questions.label: Recommendation

answers_to_specific_questions.question: Latency budget for <=10s with translation and multi-step chains?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: Indicative budget (ASSUMPTION, to be measured in spike S4): auth+transport 0.1s; merged detect+translate+classify 0.8-1.5s; deterministic tools in parallel 0.3-1.0s; relevance/explanation 1.0-2.5s; composition (structured) 1.2-3.0s; translate-out 0.8-1.5s; validation/hydration 0.2-0.4s. Typical total 5-10s; worst case exceeds 10s. Levers: merge calls, small fast models for classify/translate, parallel independent tools (history, pending orders, complementary), template-first explanations, cache welcome panel, static labels via i18n, cap candidates. Free-tier quotas make the target unreliable.
alternatives: Compose directly in the dealer's language (removes translate-out; touches D17, needs approval)
answers_to_specific_questions.label: Assumption; no benchmark run in this session

answers_to_specific_questions.question: Recommended structured response contract AI/backend/front end?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: Conceptual only. (1) Model->backend 'decision' object: schemaVersion, intent{name,confidence}, parameters, nextStep{type: tool|clarify|respond, toolName, args}, never prices or free-form facts. (2) Model composition: ordered blocks with text containing numeric slot references and productCodes/orderCodes only. (3) Backend->frontend 'response': responseId, language, blocks[] typed (text, productCards, comparison, orderSummary, purchaseList, recommendationList, welcome, clarification, notice), hydrated data, explanation reference, feedback handle, suggested next actions. (4) Stream events wrap the same blocks. Backend rejects IDs not present in this turn's tool results (provenance check) and fills digits via slots so the model cannot invent totals.
alternatives: Provider-native multi-turn tool loops (less portable across Gemini/Anthropic/OpenAI)

answers_to_specific_questions.question: How to minimise coupling with client-specific facade/core layers?
answers_to_specific_questions.recommendation: Split into extensions: uc1core (types, services, DAO, orchestrator, SPIs), uc1facades, uc1occ (yocc template), uc1backoffice, uc1sampledata (packs + generators), plus a lazy-loaded Spartacus feature library. Core talks to the client's platform through gateway SPIs (catalog, price, order, customer, stock, cart) with default implementations over OOTB services; clients override by bean alias. No client-specific models in repo. Platform version (javax vs jakarta) must be confirmed.
